title: Inline slim-span protocol and adaptive eviction controller
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's tracing path still carries per-request allocations and span serialization costs on the hotpath. Recent incidents (see postmortem link below) show tail latency regressions under traffic bursts where tracing stalls request processing. Existing efforts have focused on prefiltering and deferred sampling; this ticket targets a complementary approach: minimize binary footprint and runtime work for traces that will likely be dropped while preserving fidelity for sampled/tail flows.

Goal:
1) Implement an inline "slim-span" protocol: a compact in-memory representation optimized for the hot path (fixed-size headers, compact tag encoding, 64-bit hashed IDs) that defers heavyweight fields (stack traces, large tag blobs) to background expansion only for spans that survive sampling.
2) Add an adaptive eviction controller that uses short-window telemetry (p99 latency, per-route QPS, and span-score heuristics) to decide whether to convert slim-spans into full spans or to evict/aggregate them. Controller must operate without locks on the hotpath and avoid allocations during decision.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Slim-span format reduces heap allocations by reusing a fixed slab and encoding strings as indices into a backing string table. Trade-off: additional complexity in the background worker to rehydrate text fields.
- Eviction controller uses a bloom-ish eviction table and exponential backoff per-route to avoid oscillation. Risk: false evictions could remove useful traces; mitigations include per-route conservative mode and a sampling bias for errors.
- We avoid changing the public trace wire format; the converter produces standard spans for existing consumers. This keeps observability consumers stable but adds CPU cost on converters (background).

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (PoC): implement slim-span struct, hotpath allocation pool, and unit tests. Add metrics for allocation reductions and conversion rate. (Owner: Diego)
- Phase 2 (Pilot): add eviction controller, background rehydration worker, and opt-in route flag. Deploy to canary fleet with trace-sampling fallback enabled. Collect biz-metrics and compare p50/p99 tail latencies. (Owner: Diego + SRE)
- Phase 3 (Rollout): enable adaptive controller with gradual ramp and automatic rollback thresholds based on SLOs. Add console dashboard and alerting. (Owner: Observability team)

Acceptance criteria:
- Hotpath allocations from tracing reduced by at least 60% under synthetic workload (same request mix used by ENG-31820 benchmark).
- No measurable increase (>1%) in p50 request latency across canary traffic; p99 should reduce by >=5% in high-qps routes where sampling is enabled.
- Conversion failure rate (background rehydration errors) < 0.1% and incidents auto-roll back if >0.5%.
- Dashboard: new per-route metric "slim_span_conversion_rate", "slim_span_evictions", and "hotpath_trace_allocs" visible in Console.

Metrics to track:
- hotpath_trace_allocs (count)
- slim_span_emitted (count)
- slim_span_converted (count)
- slim_span_evicted (count)
- conversion_latency_ms (histogram)
- request latency p50/p95/p99 (before/after)

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/tracing/slim-span-protocol (draft)
- Benchmark: https://bench.redwood/internal/trace/ENG-197357 (pilot results)
- Related tickets: ENG-31820 (offload-span-encoding), ENG-142010 (sampling-pipeline-delayed-batch)
- Incident: https://incidents.redwood/2026-02-trace-stall-postmortem

2026-03-06 — Mei Patel (SRE): Added integration test harness to simulate bursty traffic; observer metrics added to sandbox.

2026-03-09 — Diego Marquez: Implemented eviction controller prototype. Chose compact bloom filter with 2-bit counters to reduce memory. Observed occasional false evicts in synthetic microbench; will add conservative thresholding per-route.
2026-03-11 — QA: End-to-end test: conversion worker recovered from a simulated DB outage; conversion backlog bounded and drained within 10s with no request impact.
2026-03-12 — Design review (Alyssa): Approved format but requested explicit backward-compatibility tests for existing downstream observability consumers.

2026-03-13 — Diego: Opening draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4602; flagged for perf review. QPS smoke on ci/presubmit shows p99 reduction on route /generate with sampling=0.2.
